newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. September housing starts, weekly jobless claims and September industrial production and utilisation data, dealers said on Thursday.
Housing starts for September is forecast to be around 1.47 million units compared with 1.525 million units reported in August.
Jobless claims for the week ending October 12 is expected to be around 331,000 against the previous week's 319,000.

Industrial production for September is expected to show a gain Of 0.1 percent from August's increase of 0.5 percent, while September capacity utilisation is expected to ease to 83.3 percent versus August's 83.5 percent.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on lack of fresh factors. Some people are waiting for possible direction from tonight's housing starts, weekly jobless claims and industrial production and capacity utilisation figures. But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday, weekend and week-fixed were unchanged from Wednesday's common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, six-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
